name: Forty Kills and a Funeral
creator: Investigative journalist Tomasz Adeyemi-Burr, self-published via gray-market feed aggregator Null Dispatch
description: A serialized true-crime investigation into the overlapping criminal ecosystems of GLMZ's mid-tiers, focusing on cases that fall into the cracks between corponation jurisdiction and city law enforcement. Each season follows a single case across twelve episodes — from the first known death to its resolution or deliberate burial — reconstructed through leaked Axiom Security incident logs, recorded testimonials from witnesses who agreed to voice distortion, and Adeyemi-Burr's own on-the-ground reporting in neighborhoods most journalists refuse to enter. The show does not sensationalize; its horror is administrative.
medium: neural feed audio / gray-market BCI aggregator
cultural_impact: Season 2's investigation into the 'Lakeward Eleven' — eleven dockworkers whose deaths were reclassified as industrial accidents by Axiom-contracted medical examiners — was shared so widely through pirated feeds that it forced a formal (and ultimately inconclusive) municipal inquiry, demonstrating that gray-market journalism could generate genuine institutional pressure.
controversy: HelixCorp's legal division filed three injunctions attempting to suppress Season 3, which investigated the disposal of failed geneware trial participants in Tier 1 districts. Adeyemi-Burr continued publishing from an undisclosed location; two of his sources were subsequently fired from their positions under unrelated pretexts.
story_hooks: Adeyemi-Burr approaches the party with a recording that implicates someone they know — and offers to suppress it in exchange for access to a source they can reach and he cannot.
A witness from Season 1 has been located by the people the show exposed; they need extraction before the next episode drops.

The show's gray-market distributor, Null Dispatch, is negotiating a corporate acquisition that would give a corponation access to all of Adeyemi-Burr's encrypted source files — and the journalist doesn't know yet.
